Optimize Images for Website Speed

Website images should be smaller than raw camera photos. This workflow helps reduce dimensions, choose modern formats, and export favicons.

Recommended workflow

  1. Resize large images to the display size needed on the page.
  2. Compress JPG/WebP output with a balanced quality value.
  3. Convert PNG photos to WebP or JPG when transparency is not needed.
  4. Keep screenshots/logos in PNG when sharp edges matter.
  5. Generate favicons from a clean square source image.

Tools used in this workflow

  • Image Resizer — Resize JPG, PNG, and WebP images online by width, height, percentage, or preset size. Fast private browser processing.
  • Image Compressor — Compress images online while controlling quality and format. See before/after file size and download optimized images instantly.
  • JPG to WebP Converter — Convert JPG photos to WebP online for faster websites and smaller file sizes.
  • PNG to WebP Converter — Convert PNG images to WebP online to reduce size while keeping good visual quality.
  • PNG to JPG Converter — Convert PNG files to JPG online with background color and quality controls for smaller image files.
  • Favicon Generator — Generate 16x16, 32x32, 48x48, 180x180, and 512x512 favicon PNG files from one image.

Why this workflow works

It follows a safe order: fix dimensions and format first, then optimize size, then verify the final output. This prevents quality loss and reduces repeated uploads.

Frequently asked questions

Should I use WebP?

WebP is usually smaller for websites and works in modern browsers.

Should I resize before compressing?

Yes, resizing first usually gives better results.
